item.description:
The library gets its plain controls: a Bin, Mark as Finished and a visible read list, saving from anywhere, saving an article again, gilt-edged favourites, better image repair and a log beside bug reports.

  • Info ▸ Actions ▸ Save again from the web fetches an article’s page afresh: new text and images replace the old, while the piece keeps its place on the stack, its category, tags, highlights and where you were. A title you’ve renamed stays yours.
  • It shows in the Save sheet like any save; if the page can’t be fetched, nothing changes and the sheet says why.
  • A favourite now shows it: a band of gold leaf along the top edge of its cover on the shelves and Today’s desk, a gold cap on its spine, and a small gold “Favourite” mark in contents lists, the stack and the Info drawer.
  • Help ▸ Report a Bug… now writes the last hour of Scribe’s log to a file and shows it in Finder beside the email draft, ready to drag in. The log says what Scribe did, not what you read: titles, links and notes are left out of it.
  • Settings ▸ Library ▸ Bin lists the pieces you’ve deleted, with when each went and how long it has left, and lets you restore one, delete it now, or empty the bin.
  • The Catalogue’s new Deleted status finds a deleted piece by search; it shows with Restore in place of opening.
  • Right-clicking a deleted piece offers Restore and Delete Now.
  • Mark as Finished and Mark as Unread, in a piece’s right-click menu, the Info drawer’s actions, the Reader menu (⇧⌘F) and the command palette. Finished sticks wherever your reading stopped; Unread forgets your place too.
  • At the end of a piece on your stack, a quiet bar offers to take it off the stack, finished, in one click.
  • A Finished option on each category’s shelf, a “Read” saved search in the Catalogue, and Today’s “N are finished” now opens the list.
  • Fixed: figures a site serves through an image proxy (Next.js, Netlify, Substack) were dropped when extraction lost them, because every one looked like the same image; they come back now.
  • Fixed: an image saved as an error page (an archive's "not found" page, say) stayed a broken frame for ever; it's fetched again from the page's own address, or taken out.
  • At the next launch every saved article's images are checked again, and from then on images that still fail are retried a few per launch, in the background, rather than once.
  • A bookmarklet (Settings ▸ Saving ▸ From your browser) saves the page you’re on; Scribe saves it quietly behind the top bar’s pill, and only opens Save if something went wrong.
  • Any app can hand Scribe a page to save with a `scribe://save?url=…` link.
  • Select a link or some text anywhere on your Mac and choose Services ▸ Save to Scribe.

A fixes release: Scribe launches and reads faster in a large library, saves your place without reloading everything, checks the library file before backing it up, refuses copy-protected and fixed-layout books with a reason, resumes interrupted saves, and reopens where you left off.

  • Fixed: every launch read the full text of every saved article for a one-time image repair that had already run. Launch now reads two small columns, and only when the repair is still owed.
  • Fixed: links were fetched with no browser identity, so some sites served a different page than Safari would, or none. Scribe now asks for pages as Safari does, in your languages.
  • Fixed: saving a very long PDF stored and indexed its whole text. PDFs now keep the same amount of searchable text as books (their first two megabytes), so the library file stays small and search stays quick.
  • Fixed: opening a large PDF or a long article read the file on the main thread, freezing the window and the reader's opening animation for a moment. Files and a book's chapters now load in the background, with the placeholder shown until they're ready.
  • Fixed: switching quickly from one piece to another could show the first piece's content in the second.
  • Fixed: Scribe saved your place on nearly every scroll step and page turn, and each save made the whole library reload behind the reader. Your place is now saved every few seconds while you read, and at once when you close a piece, switch to another, or leave Scribe.
  • Scribe now runs SQLite's quick check of the library file at launch, before the weekly backup. If the file has a problem, a notice says so and that week's backup is skipped, so the last good copy is kept.
  • Fixed: a copy-protected EPUB (from Apple Books, Adobe Digital Editions or a library's LCP loan) saved as a book of blank pages. Scribe now says it's copy-protected and can't be opened, instead of saving it.
  • Fixed-layout books (comics, picture books, some textbooks) are refused with a clear message rather than saved as badly flowed pages.
  • Fixed: quitting Scribe while a batch of links or files was still saving lost the ones that hadn't finished. The next launch now offers to resume them, from the Save sheet or the pill in the top bar.
  • Fixed: if something else had the library file open for a moment (a backup copying it, Finder, a second copy of Scribe), Scribe gave up at once. It now waits up to five seconds.
  • Developer builds: Xcode previews open a throwaway library instead of the real one, so rendering a preview can't migrate or back up your library.
  • Right-click a highlight in Highlights or the reader's notes rail and choose "Copy with Citation" to copy it as a quote with the piece's title, author, source, year and link, ready to paste.
  • Scribe now reopens on the tab, category or piece you had open when you quit. Turn this off in Settings ▸ Reading ("Open Scribe where I left off").

Shelves no longer leave their first book standing up.

  • Fixed: after clicking a shelf, its first book stayed lifted with its title showing, even with the pointer elsewhere. The keyboard highlight now shows only once you use the arrow keys or Tab to the shelf.
  • A long shelf (in the Catalogue's shelf view or a category) keeps one height as you scroll it, sized for its tallest book, instead of depending on which books are on screen.
